title: Replying to @ryanconnelly0 I was definitley mixed on this show, but I...
transcript: Alright, ask and you shall receive. Here's my full review of New York, New York. And buckle up, cause it's probably gonna be a long one. And right off the bat, I'll say what really works about the show is the actual production itself. The sets are grand, the costumes are gorgeous. And of course, it's a Susan Stroman show, so you know the dancing is going to be out of this world. There's a lot of really fun and imaginative dance sequences. There's one in particular at a construction site where they're tapping on steel beams above the city, and it's just, it's. It's spectacular. It's one of my favorite dance sequences I've seen in a while. However, I do think the book of the show and the score of the show need a lot of work. And thankfully this is the first preview, so they have plenty of time to make those changes. Um, and it's important to note that this is a show that did not do any kind of pre Broadway tryout. This is literally the first time it was put up in front of an audience. So I am sure there's going to be a lot of changes made between now and opening. In terms of what I hope they change, there's definitely some pacing things that I think can be tightened up. In Act One in particular, which is currently clocking in at an hour and 1/2, I think that there's a lot of tightening up. That can be done. Part of the problem that the show runs into is that there's just so many characters, and the show doesn't really know what to do with them all. I definitely think act 2 is better at bringing together all of the characters, but in act one, they definitely feel very disparate. They feel very separated. And for me, this really dragged down the pacing. And also because there were so many characters, I didn't really feel like each character got enough time to really feel fully developed or for the audience to buy into their individual journeys. Which brings me to the main love story, which is, like, the heart of the show. And honestly, one of my biggest gripes with it. I fundamentally did not like Colton Ryan character. And that's not a knock on Colton Ryan. I actually think he's really great in the show. I think his voice suits the style of music really well. He's really funny, he's charming. I just did not like the way his character was written. I found him to be kind of an ass. And I just like. Because I didn't like him and I wasn't rooting for him. By extension, I wasn't rooting for the love story. And if you're not rooting for the love story, which is the heart of the show, what are you rooting for? I will say, though, I think Anna Ozelle, who's the other half of that couple, is giving a Really fantastic performance as well. For me she was the highlight of the show, especially as 2 solos in act 2 that for me were my favorite songs. So overall what I recommend it. I think it depends on what you're looking for in a musical. If you're looking for a big splashy musical that that harkens back to the days of your, then yeah, I think you're gonna have a fun time with this. Like. Like I said, the production elements of the show are really great. But if you're someone who comes to the theater for the story, I don't know that the story, at least in its current form, is going to resonate with you. At least it didn't resonate for me. I think that in its current form, it's a really great production of a very mediocre at best show. Credit where credit is due, though, I think the final like 20 minutes of the show are actually really good. Um, they kind of hit in all the right ways, and I really thought that the show actually stuck the landing on the ending. So if they're able to take what made the ending work so well, and they're able to apply that to the rest of the show, I think they could have a big hit on their hands. But in its current form, it's just not quite there yet for me.
reasoning: Creator explicitly frames this as a mixed review, praising production elements (sets, costumes, choreography) but criticizing the book, score, pacing, and central love story. Recommendation is conditional on what you want from a musical.
